findings.title: Retry-count cleanup is not limited to SMS reminders
findings.body: In the initial deleteMany, the second OR branch only checks retryCount > 1. It is not scoped to method: WorkflowMethods.SMS or to unscheduled reminders, so any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders, or already scheduled reminders) with retryCount greater than 1 will be deleted. This can delete records outside the SMS retry flow. Scope the retry condition to SMS reminders, for example by putting method: WorkflowMethods.SMS at the top level of the where clause or inside the retry branch.

findings.title: Retry count increments use stale read value
findings.body: Both failure paths update retryCount to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read before the SMS attempt. If overlapping cron executions or duplicate requests process the same reminder, they can read the same retryCount and write the same new value, losing increments and preventing deletion after two failures. Use Prisma's atomic increment, e.g. retryCount: { increment: 1 }, and consider claiming rows before processing.

findings.title: Unsendable reminders are not counted as failures
findings.body: When message is empty or sendTo is falsy, the code skips scheduling without incrementing retryCount or deleting the reminder. A reminder with a missing recipient or unrenderable message will therefore be picked up repeatedly until scheduledDate passes, instead of being stopped by the new retry limit. Treat this as a failure case or delete the reminder explicitly.

findings.title: Cron authentication passes when CRON_API_KEY is undefined
findings.body: The authentication check compares process.env.CRON_API_KEY with the supplied key. If CRON_API_KEY is not set and no key is supplied, both values are undefined, so process.env.CRON_API_KEY !== apiKey is false and the request is accepted. The handler should reject requests when the environment key is missing or empty, and compare against a configured secret.
